plain.4: The drawer creaks open to reveal a stack of yellowed paper, and beneath a faded receipt lies a photograph that seems to hold its breath. My fingers tremble as I lift the brittle edges, revealing a crisp image of my grandmother standing in a sun-drenched garden, her smile bright against the soft blue sky. The colors are washed out by time, yet the warmth of that afternoon still radiates from the glass, pulling me back to a summer I barely remember. A sudden, sharp ache blooms in my chest, a physical echo of the joy captured in those frozen seconds. I press the photo gently against my palm, feeling the ghost of her laughter through the decades.
